correctness.rationale: The actual 2026-11-08 RESULT defines A=V⊕kz with multiplication B_lambda(v,w)z, V=k^n⊕k^n and lambda≠0. Since A²=kz, every homomorphism has block form (T,ell,alpha). The complete multiplicativity and idempotence equations are B(Tv,Tw)=alpha B(v,w), T²=T, alpha²=alpha, ell T+alpha ell=ell. For alpha=1, nondegeneracy of B forces T invertible; T²=T yields T=I and ell=0. For alpha=0, W=im T is totally two-sided B-isotropic, dim W=r≤n and ell factors through T. Each r-plane W has exactly q^{r(2n-r)} projection complements and q^r central graph shifts, hence E_r=q^{r(2n-r+1)} times its isotropic-plane count; the only other rank is full 2n+1. If lambda²≠1, the two ordered equations p+lambda p_rev=0 and p_rev+lambda p=0 force p=p_rev=0. The coordinate projections X,Y of W obey X⊥Y and a+b≤n. Their Goursat kernels have common quotient dimension t=a+b-r and are parametrized by Gaussian choices for X,Y, kernels and GL_t isomorphisms, yielding the stated finite sum. For odd lambda=1, the form is split symmetric: hyperbolic-orthogonal frame counts give [n r]_q ∏(q^{n-i-1}+1). For lambda=-1 (including even characteristic lambda=1) the form is alternating: symplectic frames give ∏(q^{2(n-i)}-1)/(q^{r-i}-1). Edge cases r=0,n, n=1, q=2 and q=4 are consistent; no claimed prime-field-only assumption. As independent finite corroboration, a new RREF checker counted all bilinear-isotropic subspaces for n=2 in F3 (lambda 1,2), F4 (lambda 1,2), and F5 (lambda 1,2,4), plus n=1 in F7. Each matched exact formulas; an independent direct 3×3 matrix map check tested multiplication on every basis pair and F²=F for n=1 and five (q,lambda) pairs: (3,1),(3,2),(5,1),(5,2),(5,4), reproducing rank counts [1,18,0,1], [1,36,0,1], [1,50,0,1], [1,50,0,1], [1,150,0,1]. The finite tests are only corroboration for the universal algebraic proof.

value.rationale: Idempotent algebra endomorphisms are natural retracts, and their full image-rank spectrum is a meaningful invariant of a coherent infinite family of central-sum associative algebras. The generic nonsymmetric lambda²!=1 regime requires simultaneous two-sided isotropy, not merely the known symplectic constraint, and yields a nontrivial Goursat/Gaussian formula whose maximal proper rank n has ∑_{a=0}^n[n a]_q possible image spaces. The symmetric and alternating phases form mathematically motivated boundary comparisons with different rank multiplicities (e.g. q=5,n=2: rank-2 map counts 125000, 187500, 2437500), while proper rank n+1..2n is impossible. This is a natural all-dimension, all-prime-power classification with independently useful exact counts, not an arbitrary small-instance table. Standard frame counts and the previously covered alternating subclass are explicitly excluded from claims of new technique or priority.
